article.title: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 Fix Two Critical Unauthenticated RCE Flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
article.summary: PHP's security release names the two CVSS 9.2 flaws as CVE-2026-109618 (OOM corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state), fixed in four branches.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

The security release the PHP project [pre-announced on October 20](/article/2026-10/21-php-pre-announces-october-21-security-release-for-two-critical-vulnerabilities-rated-cvss-v40-92) shipped on October 21, 2026. According to the [PHP.net announcement](https://www.php.net/index.php), PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 "fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution." The notice says: "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice."

## What We Know

The questions the pre-announcement left open are now answered by the release notice and by two advisories in the php-src repository.

- **CVE-2026-109618, "RCE via OOM corruption."** The [advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) states that "PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors." In some contexts request memory is reachable before it is fully initialized, and an allocation failure at that point leaves it in an invalid state that request shutdown may then read.
- **CVE-2026-109619, "RCE via stale global state."** The [advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) describes global state that a worker retains but that points to memory owned by one request, leading to a use after free. It says: "The demonstrated producing and consuming operations occur in different HTTP requests handled by the same worker."
- **Severity.** Both advisories list the severity as Critical with a CVSS score of 9.2, matching the figure in the earlier notice.
- **Affected and fixed versions.** Both advisories list affected versions below 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12, and name those four releases as the patched versions.
- **Older branches.** PHP.net says PHP 8.1 and older "no longer receive updates from the PHP project," but that the security team "provided minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4 , PHP 8.0 , and PHP 8.1" for people building from source. It adds that Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance. It also notes that PHP 8.2 reaches end of life on 31 December 2026.
- **PHP 8.6.** The PHP.net notice says PHP 8.6.0 RC4, also announced on October 21, contains the fixes, and that the next release candidate, RC5, is planned for 5 November 2026.

## Who Is Exposed

PHP.net says the risk applies to "all PHP installations serving web requests," and lists PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. It says it considers the risk highest for mod_php, "with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs."

The [OOM advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) explains the mod_php difference: Apache mod_php "unconditionally invokes the request shutdown procedure, even when request startup has failed." By contrast, "FPM exits the child when request startup fails," and the advisory says that "no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI." It states that complete remote code execution "was validated over HTTP against mod_php with default PHP input and memory limits."

For the stale-state flaw, the [second advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) calls a PHP 8.5 fatal-error backtrace case "the strongest demonstrated case" and the basis of the confirmed mod_php exploitation. It also lists a session upload progress case as confirmed.

## Interim Mitigations

[PHP.net](https://www.php.net/index.php) lists measures for operators who cannot update at once, while saying they "reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe."

- For CVE-2026-109618: set `memory_limit=-1`, ideally where applications cannot override it, and use a low `post_max_size`; the notice suggests 8M for applications without file uploads and 32M where uploads are required. It warns against substituting `RLIMIT_AS` or `RLIMIT_DATA`.
- For CVE-2026-109619: set `session.upload_progress.enabled=0` and restart every worker. On PHP 8.5, set `fatal_error_backtraces=0`.

The stale-state advisory adds that changing `error_reporting`, using `@`, or disabling `display_errors` or `log_errors` "does not protect against this vulnerability."

## What We Don't Know

- The sources reviewed do not say whether either flaw has been exploited in the wild.
- The OOM advisory states that exploit portability and reliability depend on the PHP build, extensions, frontend behavior and allocator layout, so the practical exposure of a given installation is not fully characterized.
- Package availability varies by distribution; PHP.net directs users to check their vendor.
